newsitem.title: CANADA: CP Rail deal speeds oat shipments to U.S..
newsitem.headline: CP Rail deal speeds oat shipments to U.S..

text.p: A deal between CP Rail System and General Mills to make dedicated freight runs between the Canadian prairies and Minneapolis this fall has alleviated harvest storage pressure and sharply cut railcar turnarounds.

"I don't know if it can be done for all commodities because General Mills has a lot of storage capacity, but it really helped out at harvest time," Manitoba Pool Elevators oat trader Len Karnafel told Reuters.
Six designated 100-car unit trains have completed the run since the pilot project began last month, CP Rail spokesman Ian La Couvee said in a phone interview from Calgary.
"We've reduced cycle times (freight train turnaround) by 50 percent," La Couvee said.

Each week, a designated train loaded oats at elevators of Saskatchewan Wheat Pool, Pioneer Grain Co Ltd, Manitoba Pool Elevators and N.M. Paterson & Sons Ltd in Manitoba and Saskatchewan, La Couvee said.
"They give you 10 days warning of when the train's coming so you can arrange with your producers for on-time delivery," said Pioneer's oat production manager Doug Fisher.
"The trains are guaranteed. Everything moves in one train to General Mills," he said. "It's been working fantastic."

"The dedicated trains allow our three Minneapolis elevators to better plan and schedule unloading. We're also able to turn the railcars back to CP more quickly," General Mills oat operations manager Rick Cole said in a statement.
The arrangement has also aided Canadian oat exports.
Total exports of Canadian oats on October 27 stood at 380,500 tonnes, up 36 percent from 280,300 tonnes at the same time last year, Canadian Grain Commission statistics show.
Oat output in crop year 1996/97 (August/July) was estimated at 4.57 million tonnes, up 60 percent from last year's 2.86 million tonnes, according to Statistics Canada.
